yaml.title: Text Mining UN General Debates (1946-2024)
yaml.author: Shuhei Kuwabara
yaml.description: Analyzing thematic shifts in 10,000+ UN speeches using LDA Topic Modeling and PCA.

markdown.markdown:
This project applies **Natural Language Processing (NLP)** techniques to analyze the evolution of international diplomatic discourse. Using a corpus of **10,952 speeches** from the UN General Assembly (1946–2024), the analysis explores how global priorities have shifted from post-war security concerns to modern sustainability agendas. **Academic Context:** Submitted as the W11+1 Summative Assessment for **DS202A: Data Science for Social Scientists** at the **London School of Economics (LSE)**. ## Access the Files ```{=html}
View Full Analysis Report Comprehensive report including Text Similarity & LDA Topic Modeling.
Source Code (.qmd) Raw Quarto file containing the reproducible R code.
``` ## Methodology By combining unsupervised learning with dimensionality reduction, this analysis uncovers macro-level trends in diplomatic history. ### 1. Corpus Analysis & Anomaly Detection Using TF-IDF weighting and Cosine Similarity on a corpus of 10,952 speeches, I detected "Structural Anomalies" (e.g., historical verbosity peaks around 1960) and "Semantic Anomalies" where specific speeches significantly diverged from established national rhetorical styles. ### 2. Topic Modeling (LDA) I applied **Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA)** with Gibbs sampling (k=8) to identify latent themes. The model successfully distinguished between historical topics like Decolonization/Apartheid and contemporary issues such as Climate Change/Sustainable Development. ### 3. Dimensionality Reduction (PCA) Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied to the topic proportions to visualize temporal trajectories: - PC1: Illustrated a shift from "Security & Institutions" to "Governance & Sustainability". - PC2: Captured the rise and fall of "Geopolitical Conflict," peaking during the Cold War era (1970s/80s). ## Tech Stack R NLP (quanteda) LDA (topicmodels) PCA Unsupervised Learning ggplot2
